The workspace was read-only and shell access failed, so I could not persist `research-materials.md` or `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The following provisional units should be appended after RC069.

### Chapter 2B

- **RC070** — IPAC’s 13 July 2022 Papua report found increasing attacks and civilian victims by both TPNPB and security forces; weapons were obtained through raids, cross-border purchases, and illegal sales by rogue security personnel. It found troop deployments ineffective and called for civilian protection, accountability, and training. Attribution is institutional/security-policy based, not a personal order. Lenses: 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.7, 2B.9, 2B.10. [IPAC report](https://understandingconflict.org/id/publications/escalating-armed-conflict-and-a-new-security-approach-in-papua), lines 24–30.

- **RC071** — ASEAN’s 11 November 2022 leaders’ review recorded “little progress” implementing the Five-Point Consensus, continuing violence, and the need for measurable indicators and timelines. This is contrary evidence on diplomatic efficacy, while also documenting a formal regional process. It does not establish Widodo’s personal failure because implementation depended on ASEAN and Myanmar actors. Lenses: 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.10. [ASEAN review](https://asean.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/06-ASEAN-Leaders-Review-and-Decision-on-the-Implementation-of-the-Five-Point-Consensus_fin.pdf), pp. 1–2.

- **RC072** — HRW reported that ASEAN had failed to fulfill its pledges or achieve tangible results after a year, while Indonesia and other states publicly criticized Myanmar’s obstruction. This separates Indonesia’s diplomatic activity from the broader consensus’s limited outcome. Lenses: 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.10. [HRW assessment](https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/04/22/myanmar-aseans-failed-5-point-consensus-year), lines 594–609.

### Chapter 3B

- **RC073** — Komnas HAM’s 2022 annual report records rapid responses to Wadas, alleged police violence, Kanjuruhan, and other serious incidents. This is evidence that an independent national commission remained operational and investigated rights issues, but not proof that remedies were effective. Lenses: 3B.9, 3B.10. [Komnas HAM annual report](https://www.komnasham.go.id/index.php/laporan/2023/07/17/112/laporan-tahunan-komnas-ham-ri-tahun-2022.html), lines 75–84.

- **RC074** — Reporting on the 2022 Sexual Violence Crimes Law records Widodo’s early-2022 request to accelerate protection legislation and the law’s expanded offenses, victim coverage, and restitution/counseling provisions. Advocates simultaneously warned that reporting barriers and inadequate law-enforcement training would limit protection. This supports formal policy action plus contrary implementation evidence. Lenses: 3B.5, 3B.7, 3B.10. [TIME report](https://time.com/6166853/indonesia-sexual-violence-law/), lines 112–118 and 133–149.

- **RC075** — Indonesia’s later UN human-rights submission states that six soldiers were convicted by military court for the 2022 Mimika killings after an investigation into an illegal firearms transaction. Because the source is retrospective and government-presented, it establishes a formal accountability outcome but not independent remedy effectiveness or presidential knowledge. Lenses: 3B.1, 3B.9, 3B.10. [UN document](https://docstore.ohchr.org/SelfServices/FilesHandler.ashx?enc=QLPP40nzXuToiSCfvww5xhEtEgkQKtlSB2ZP5ZuvgtsdukPEW14NaiRUXgn9n266KocAYmIP9qNJ%2FVelmcUP6A%3D%3D), pp. 8–9, paras. 45–46.

### Chapter 4B

- **RC076** — Bawaslu’s September 2022 record shows it adjudicated an administrative complaint by Partai Pelita and rejected it because the same subject had already been examined and decided. This is event-level evidence that electoral oversight operated during the period, but it does not prove full independence or executive noninterference. Lenses: 4B.1, 4B.4, 4B.8. [Bawaslu record](https://www.bawaslu.go.id/id/berita/objek-permohonan-sudah-pernah-diperiksa-bawaslu-tolak-permohonan-partai-pelita).

- **RC077** — Contemporary reporting on the December 2022 Criminal Code states that implementation regulations were still required, that the Code would not take effect immediately, and that civil-society groups intended constitutional litigation. Critics warned of selective enforcement affecting poorer or politically vulnerable people. Lenses: 4B.2, 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.7, 4B.10. [TIME report](https://time.com/6238952/indonesia-criminal-code-to-ban-sex-outside-marriage/), lines 7–10 and 19–22.

### Chapter 5B

- **RC078** — BPK’s 2022 audit summary found Rp25.85 trillion in findings, including uneconomic, inefficient, ineffective, and noncompliant management. It identified uncertified land across 33 highway roads and Rp10.49 trillion in incomplete state-equity-funded works. This is adverse implementation and infrastructure-governance evidence, not proof of personal presidential misconduct. Lenses: 5B.5, 5B.7, 5B.10, 8B.4, 8B.7. [BPK audit summary](https://www.bpk.go.id/news/bpk-gives-unqualified-opinion-on-2022-financial-statements-of-central-government), lines 43–52.

- **RC079** — The World Bank’s retrospective Indonesia evaluation found capacity gains in local governments and water utilities, but lagging urban and subnational infrastructure because of weak local capacity; it also found domestic-revenue mobilization stalled amid political sensitivity and procurement complexity. This provides balanced implementation evidence with substantial shared-authority and retrospective limitations. Lenses: 5B.3, 5B.5, 5B.7, 5B.9, 8B.4, 8B.7. [World Bank evaluation](https://ieg.worldbankgroup.org/evaluations/world-bank-group-indonesia).

### Chapter 6B

- **RC080** — Indonesia’s official 2022 stunting report states that prevalence fell from 24.4% to 21.6%, but the 2.8-point reduction missed the 3.4-point annual target. The report attributes implementation to central and subnational governments and stresses continuing monitoring and evaluation. Lenses: 6B.1, 6B.3, 6B.6, 6B.9, 6B.10. [Official stunting indicators](https://stunting.go.id/hasil-perhitungan-ikps-nasional-dan-provinsi-tahun-2022/), lines 33–40.

- **RC081** — The same report records that immunization and modern family-planning coverage were only about 67%, while skilled-facility childbirth coverage was about 90%. These are population-level coverage constraints that qualify broad human-development gains; they cannot be assigned personally to Widodo without delivery-chain evidence. Lenses: 6B.1, 6B.3, 6B.4, 6B.9. [Official stunting indicators](https://stunting.go.id/hasil-perhitungan-ikps-nasional-dan-provinsi-tahun-2022/), lines 45–56.

- **RC082** — The 2022 implementation report describes cross-sectoral central, regional, academic, private-sector, media, and community participation, with routine monitoring intended to identify barriers and refine implementation. This supports coordinated policy design but makes attribution to the president alone inappropriate. Lenses: 6B.4, 6B.6, 6B.9, 6B.10. [2022 implementation report](https://stunting.go.id/en/executive-report-accelerating-the-reduction-of-stunting-year-2022/), lines 30–38.

### Chapter 7B

- **RC083** — KPK’s 2022 integrity-survey release describes prevention measures including recurring anti-corruption training, IT-based prevention systems, and protected complaint channels. This is favorable institutional safeguard evidence, not evidence of Widodo’s personal honesty or direct corrective action. Lenses: 7B.6, 7B.7, 7B.10. [KPK integrity-survey release](https://www.kpk.go.id/id/ruang-informasi/berita/kpk-rilis-hasil-survei-integritas-tahun-2022).

- **RC084** — BPK’s audit of KPK’s 2022 accounts found an unqualified opinion and no significant financial-statement problem, while identifying weaknesses in seized-asset administration, procurement compliance, and the national anti-corruption strategy’s institutional procedures. This supplies both safeguard and adverse institutional evidence, but no personal nexus. Lenses: 7B.6, 7B.7, 7B.10. [BPK KPK audit](https://www.bpk.go.id/news/selesaikan-pemeriksaan-bpk-serahkan-lhp-atas-lk-kpk-tahun-2022), lines 47–70.

- **RC085** — Searches for 2022 personal enrichment, family benefit, beneficial-ownership concealment, or direct presidential obstruction did not recover a verified finding. Disposition: `unresolved`, not adverse evidence. Existing disclosure material remains usable only as a record of declared assets.

### Chapter 8B

- **RC086** — The World Bank retrospective evaluation found that its Indonesia portfolio helped build local-government and water-utility capacity, but broader urban and subnational infrastructure lagged because of weak subnational capacity. This is a mixed implementation result, not a durable national effectiveness finding attributable solely to Widodo. Lenses: 8B.2, 8B.4, 8B.7. [World Bank evaluation](https://ieg.worldbankgroup.org/evaluations/world-bank-group-indonesia).

- **RC087** — BPK’s 2022 audit identified incomplete highway land certification and incomplete state-equity-funded works, providing concrete contrary evidence against treating infrastructure spending or approvals as successful delivery. Lenses: 8B.2, 8B.4, 8B.7. [BPK audit summary](https://www.bpk.go.id/news/bpk-gives-unqualified-opinion-on-2022-financial-statements-of-central-government), lines 47–52.

- **RC088** — The official 2022 stunting report explicitly states that implementation required routine joint monitoring and evaluation and that the year’s reduction missed the stated target. This supports a mixed effectiveness record and a concrete correction/monitoring need, without assigning the shortfall personally to Widodo. Lenses: 8B.2, 8B.4, 8B.6, 8B.7. [Official implementation report](https://stunting.go.id/en/executive-report-accelerating-the-reduction-of-stunting-year-2022/), lines 33–38.

### Dispositions

- RC070–RC084 and RC086–RC088: proposed `final_evidence`.
- RC085: `unresolved`, not negative evidence.
- The Bawaslu page was retained as a final candidate based on the searchable result text; if the underlying page cannot be independently retrieved in the local evidence workflow, downgrade it to `discovery_only`.
- No new evidence established personal enrichment, direct human-rights orders, command responsibility, or independently verified durable program success.
- Remaining gaps are concentrated in local-language primary records, project-level audits, regional service quality, direct presidential election-delay evidence, and the personal/network integrity nexus.
